title: This Time, I'll Follow Your Lead
teaser: This time on the surgical schedule, Sakaguchi is the primary surgeon and Mido is first assistant.
gallery_caption: This Time, I'll Follow Your Lead

choices.choice_em2_b1_a: "Dr. Mido, return it to its resting position first. We follow my sequence on this case."
choices.choice_em2_b1_b: "Are you used to fanning out the mesentery first? Tell me your reasoning."
choices.choice_em2_b1_c: "That exposes the mesentery very clearly. Ease back for a moment, though—let's divide the steps."
choices.choice_em2_d2_a: Set out a middle-ground check that preserves the isolation field, and make the call to release artificial elevation first.
choices.choice_em2_d2_b: Have Mido lay out her exact risk concerns first, address each one with concrete safeguards, then make the call.
choices.choice_em2_d2_c: Assign clear two-person roles to shield the bowel ends and trace the mesenteric root together before making the call.
choices.choice_em2_f3_a: "What about the twelve points you took off? While we're still at the table, you might as well give me the rest."
choices.choice_em2_f3_b: "Earning three extra points from Chief Mido is no small feat—I'll gladly take an eighty-eight."
choices.choice_em2_f3_c: "Now that the primary surgeon has his score—care to hear how I'd grade my first assistant today?"

nodes.em2_001: Having completed a standard surgical scrub, Ryuji Sakaguchi held both hands raised in front of his chest, stepped onto the foot sensor outside Operating Room 2, and walked through the sliding doors.
nodes.em2_002: When he checked the scheduling whiteboard that morning for today's elective open segmental small-bowel resection, the first-assistant slot had still been marked pending—until half an hour ago during his final pre-op ward check, when he heard the surgical chief had picked up the marker and written her own name in.
nodes.em2_003: Beneath the shadowless lamps, Hiroko Sugimura had already laid out the laparotomy and gastrointestinal anastomosis instruments in crisp order across the sterile back table. Seeing Sakaguchi enter, she held out a folded sterile towel, then opened a long-sleeved sterile gown.
nodes.em2_004: Sakaguchi dried his hands and slipped his arms into the sleeves while Moe Honjo stepped over from the circulating side to tie the back strings, before Hiroko gloved both of his hands.
nodes.em2_005: He stepped up to the primary surgeon's spot and raised his eyes toward Emiko Mido—already fully gowned and gloved, standing quietly directly across the table in the first-assistant position.
nodes.em2_006: Their gazes met for a beat across the green sterile drapes. Mindful of the awake patient behind the head-side screen, Sakaguchi lowered his voice half a notch.
nodes.em2_009: "You didn't misread the positions, did you?"
nodes.em2_011: "I just didn't expect the surgical chief to write her own name into my first-assistant column."
nodes.em2_012: "Did you think I didn't know how to assist?"
nodes.em2_013: "At Hoshimi, at least, I haven't seen you assist anyone yet."
nodes.em2_015: Above her surgical mask, those cool eyes held not a trace of humor. Her gloved hands hovered neatly inside the sterile zone at her chest, yet her presence felt every bit as commanding as when she stood in the primary spot herself.
nodes.em2_018: Behind the instrument table, Hiroko Sugimura caught that crisp exchange, let her gaze flick briefly between the two surgeons, and quietly moved a belly-bladed skin scalpel to the front row within easiest reach.
nodes.em2_019: Beside the head-end monitor, Moe Honjo finished checking the blood-pressure cuff, pulse-oximeter clip, and IV drip rate, gave the female patient's hand a gentle reassuring pat behind the ether screen, and looked up to call out the pre-incision time-out:
nodes.em2_020: "Patient identity confirmed: forty-year-old female with a localized benign small-bowel stricture and recurrent intermittent partial obstruction, scheduled for elective open segmental small-bowel resection and end-to-end anastomosis. Pre-op preparation and epidural block level confirmed; vital signs stable."
nodes.em2_021: From behind the sterile screen came the patient's slightly self-conscious but steady voice.
nodes.em2_022: "Thank you, Doctors, Nurses... As long as it stops cramping up every time I eat like it's been doing lately, I'll cooperate however you need."
nodes.em2_023: Sakaguchi answered toward the head of the table in a warm, clear voice.
nodes.em2_024: "The epidural block is already working, so you won't feel sharp pain at the incision. If you notice any deep tugging in your abdomen or any nausea during the procedure, tell Nurse Honjo right by your head at any time and we'll adjust right away."
nodes.em2_026: Sakaguchi brought his gaze back to the abdominal field bathed in the shadowless light and extended his right hand toward the Mayo stand.
nodes.em2_029: Through a right mid-to-lower paramedian incision, he divided skin, subcutaneous tissue, and the anterior rectus sheath in clean sequence, touching cautery to two tiny subcutaneous bleeders; after retracting the rectus muscle laterally, he incised the posterior sheath and peritoneum to enter the peritoneal cavity smoothly.
nodes.em2_030: There was no denying it—as a first assistant, Emiko Mido's hands were astonishingly exact.
nodes.em2_031: The instant the tips of Sakaguchi's scissors tented the peritoneum, her toothed forceps across the table had already picked up the matching point at identical height; the moment the wound edges parted, she had already taken warm saline laparotomy pads from Hiroko and neatly lined both margins of the abdominal wall.
nodes.em2_032: Sakaguchi slipped his hand gently into the abdomen, running the small bowel methodically loop by loop until he located the localized ileal stricture responsible for her recurrent partial obstructions and cradled it smoothly up onto the wound pads.
nodes.em2_033: The narrowed segment measured roughly three centimeters, its serosa thickened with chronic fibrosis; the proximal bowel was mildly dilated and hypertrophied from prolonged impaired emptying, while the distal limb lay comparatively collapsed and slender.
nodes.em2_034: "Stricture localized cleanly—serosa is smooth, with no sign of malignancy or dense adhesions. First I'll check the proximal and distal orientation down to the mesenteric root in its resting position—"
nodes.em2_035: Before he had even finished speaking, Emiko Mido's hands were already moving across the table.
nodes.em2_036: Out of sheer muscle memory forged from years of operating as sole lead, she cradled both ends of the bowel loop through warm moist gauze and turned her wrists, flipping the entire diseased segment briskly to the right of the incision and drawing the underlying small-bowel mesentery into a taut, flat fan.
nodes.em2_037: Her motion was crisp and her tension well within safe limits—yet the natural resting lie of the proximal and distal limbs had been transformed in an instant into a windowing posture ready for immediate vascular ligation.
nodes.em2_038: The air over the table paused for half a beat.
nodes.em2_039: Hiroko's hand stilled at the edge of the tray with a right-angle clamp, her eyes darting instinctively toward Sakaguchi in the primary spot.
nodes.em2_040: Rather than cutting along the plane she had already set up for him, Sakaguchi calmly lifted his gaze to the woman across the table.
nodes.em2_041: "Dr. Mido, return it to its resting position first. We follow my sequence on this case."
nodes.em2_042: Mido's wrists stopped where they were, her brows knitting almost imperceptibly above her mask.
nodes.em2_043: "We'll divide the mesenteric vessels soon enough, but before flipping the loop, I want to see the transition zone from the dilated proximal bowel to healthy wall and verify the natural lie at the mesenteric root without tension. Flipping it early scrambles the native anatomical reference."
nodes.em2_044: For two seconds their eyes locked.
nodes.em2_045: Mido studied his gaze as if weighing whether he was clinging to rigid textbook dogma or operating from real method. Half a beat later, without a word, she eased her wrists back and laid the small bowel smoothly into its original resting orientation.
nodes.em2_046: "...Fine. It's back in resting position. Check it."
nodes.em2_047: Sakaguchi paused his exploring hand and, instead of snapping an order, asked a brief question.
nodes.em2_048: "When you resect small bowel, do you usually fan the mesentery flat right from the start?"
nodes.em2_049: "Transilluminating the primary and secondary arcades straight away is the most direct read. Sets the resection lines faster."
nodes.em2_050: "It does show the vascular arcades at a glance. This proximal limb is noticeably thickened from chronic dilation, though—before anything gets flipped around, I want to confirm the natural lie at the mesenteric root and measure our resection span in situ so we aren't hunting for orientation when we bring the ends together."
nodes.em2_051: He lightly tapped the serosa on the proximal side.
nodes.em2_052: "Ease it back for half a minute while I verify the lie. Once the resection lines are marked, open the fan at that exact angle you just used."
nodes.em2_053: Mido glanced at the hypertrophied proximal bowel wall, gave the slightest nod, and smoothly returned her wrists to neutral.
nodes.em2_055: Sakaguchi glanced across the small-bowel vascular arcades she had spread crystal-clear under the light and gave a brief nod first.
nodes.em2_056: "That's a textbook exposure of the mesenteric fan—every vascular branch reads at a glance."
nodes.em2_058: "Half a step later. Your hands were fast enough to skip straight to mesenteric division—ease the loop halfway back down first and keep the dilated proximal bowel from slipping into the cavity while I trace its natural lie from the mesenteric root. Once that's confirmed, bring the fan right back up the way you had it."
nodes.em2_059: It acknowledged her seasoned exposure skill while reclaiming control of the timing without the slightest ambiguity.
nodes.em2_060: A flicker crossed Mido's eyes; after half a beat, she let off half the tension and cradled the proximal limb steady.
nodes.em2_062: Sakaguchi gently traced from the root of the small-bowel mesentery out toward the bowel margin, confirming there was no malrotation or deep tethering adhesion along the loop, then placed sterile gauze markers at well-perfused healthy bowel wall proximal and distal to the stricture.
nodes.em2_063: "Orientation confirmed. Dr. Mido, bring the mesenteric fan up now."
nodes.em2_064: Applying even tension with both hands, Mido reproduced that flat, translucent fan with pinpoint precision, presenting the marginal vascular arcade of the segment to be resected squarely beneath the overhead lights.
nodes.em2_065: Without a superfluous word, the boundary between who set the operative sequence and who delivered the optimal field had clicked cleanly into place.
nodes.em2_066: Working along both planned resection lines, the operation moved into dividing the mesentery and excising the stenotic segment.
nodes.em2_067: Standing behind the Mayo table, Hiroko followed every movement on the field intently. Assisting Chief Mido usually meant racing half a beat ahead on every instrument pass; today, with Sakaguchi leading and Mido assisting, the table settled into a different kind of composed, interlocking precision.
nodes.em2_070: Two fine curved clamps scored the translucent serosa across avascular mesenteric windows, clamped each vessel branch in opposing pairs, and Metzenbaum scissors divided cleanly between them.
nodes.em2_072: Hiroko passed the silk tie and Sakaguchi laid down square knots with unhurried steadiness; the instant each knot snugged flat, Mido's suture scissors glided in from across the table and snipped the tails right above the knot without a wasted millimeter.
nodes.em2_073: As they neared the final vasa recta beside the proximal bowel margin to be preserved, Mido noticed Sakaguchi did not sweep straight across the wedge base as routine dictated. Instead, he deliberately slowed half a beat, switched to fine dissecting forceps, teased back a wisp of loose areolar fat along the inner edge of the marginal arcade, and preserved one slender straight vessel sitting right outside the transection line.
nodes.em2_074: "That small vessel sits right against the line. Taking it with the tie saves two minutes."
nodes.em2_075: Sakaguchi's knot-tying rhythm did not falter.
nodes.em2_076: "The proximal wall is already mildly thickened and edematous from chronic obstruction. Sparing one extra marginal straight vessel gives the antimesenteric border of our anastomosis a little more perfusion reserve."
nodes.em2_077: Mido looked down at the brisk, rosy serosal color of the preserved bowel end and offered no rebuttal.
nodes.em2_078: "...Hiroko. Moist isolation pads and atraumatic bowel clamps ready."
nodes.em2_079: Hiroko glanced to Sakaguchi first; catching his confirming nod, she briskly handed across two folded warm-saline isolation pads and four bowel clamps.
nodes.em2_080: "Isolation pads up. Come to think of it, hearing Chief Mido call ahead for setup instruments on the primary surgeon's behalf is quite a rare sight."
nodes.em2_082: Hiroko's eyes curved warmly above her mask:
nodes.em2_084: Thick warm-saline laparotomy pads were tucked snugly beneath the segment to be excised, walling off the peritoneal cavity and wound edges. Rubber-shod atraumatic bowel clamps gently occluded the preserved proximal and distal limbs, while crushing clamps secured the specimen side.
nodes.em2_085: Sakaguchi divided both ends of the bowel cleanly between the clamps, lifted out the diseased segment with its firm fibrotic ring and wedge of mesentery into the specimen basin Hiroko held to the side, and gently wiped the mucosal rims of both open lumens using small sponges moistened with sterile warm saline.
nodes.em2_086: Up to that point, the resection had proceeded with crisp efficiency, the field around the isolation pads staying clean and thoroughly controlled.
nodes.em2_087: Once the specimen basin was passed off to the non-sterile side, the overhead lights centered on the proximal and distal small-bowel ends held in the two atraumatic clamps.
nodes.em2_088: Next came the step that would decide the success of the entire operation—the pre-anastomotic safety verification and hand-sewn end-to-end anastomosis.
nodes.em2_089: Holding the shanks of both atraumatic clamps steadily, Mido used the height of the thick moist pads packed underneath to bring the two bowel ends neatly into apposition at the center of the superficial isolation plane, her gaze sweeping both mesenteric borders and the color of the bowel wall.
nodes.em2_090: "The isolation field is clean, and visibility right over the incision is rock-steady. Let's verify mesenteric alignment, cut-edge perfusion, and apposition tension right here on this pad layer—once confirmed, place stay sutures and start the posterior seromuscular interrupted row without flipping the bowel up and down again."
nodes.em2_091: Sakaguchi did not call for stay sutures right away, his eyes resting on the two bowel limbs propped high at wound level by the thick stack of pads.
nodes.em2_092: "Hold on. The safety check is non-negotiable, but we shouldn't sign off on it while the ends are propped up on thick pads like this."
nodes.em2_093: Hiroko's fingers paused slightly over the suture pack.
nodes.em2_094: Mido lifted her eyes across the table to Sakaguchi, her tone cool and direct.
nodes.em2_095: "You can see cut-edge serosal color and vasa recta pulsations at a glance right here, and the ends meet without tugging. Why disturb a stable exposure plane?"
nodes.em2_096: Keeping his eyes on the elevated bowel ends, Sakaguchi stated his assessment plainly:
nodes.em2_097: "They look effortless to bring together right now because two thick wet pads underneath are propping them up to wound level. The loop was turned during dissection, and the proximal wall is heavier than the distal limb—if we don't take off that artificial upward support and verify the natural lie from the mesenteric root first, a propped-up field can easily mask subtle mesenteric twist and hidden retraction tension until we drop the anastomosis back into the abdomen."
nodes.em2_098: Mido did not yield lightly, countering immediately from the equally sound standpoint of field stability and contamination control:
nodes.em2_099: "I understand the mechanics, but two freshly opened bowel lumens are being kept clear of the cavity solely by this isolation layer. If you pull the pads out and drop the clamps deeper to trace the root, the sterile barrier loosens—if a clamp shifts or an open lumen brushes adjacent tissue, the risk of peritoneal contamination or traction bleeding outweighs checking in place."
nodes.em2_100: The atmosphere around the table tightened in an instant.
nodes.em2_101: Both surgeons agreed completely that perfusion, orientation, and tension had to be verified before sewing; their disagreement lay in the sequence and method. Mido prioritized preserving the intact isolation barrier, field stability, and contamination control; Sakaguchi prioritized removing artificial elevation to confirm true anatomical lie and tension. Both positions rested on solid surgical reasoning—and it fell to the primary surgeon to make a call that honored both.
nodes.em2_102: Meeting Mido's sharp gaze, Sakaguchi laid out a concrete approach that safeguarded the isolation barrier while still checking the true resting lie:
nodes.em2_103: "We don't pull the main isolation pads underneath, and we don't drop the open lumens back into the deep cavity. First I'll cap both cut rims snugly with fresh moist sponges; you keep both atraumatic clamps locked and steady in your hands, simply easing off the upward lift so I can trace the natural orientation down to the mesenteric root, then verify perfusion and apposition tension right on the pad without upward traction."
nodes.em2_104: Mido's gaze sharpened slightly as she ran through the mechanics of that sequence in her head.
nodes.em2_105: "That way the isolation barrier stays intact, and we don't leave any hidden rotational tension waiting for us at closure. I'm primary on this table—we verify orientation and tension this way first, then bolster the pad and place the first stitch."
nodes.em2_106: He hadn't pulled rank for ego's sake; he had addressed her contamination concern head-on while holding firm on his own surgical threshold.
nodes.em2_107: After a one-second silence, Mido lowered her wrists cleanly with the clamps in hand, taking off the upward propping force.
nodes.em2_108: "...Isolation plane's intact. Upward lift is off—run your check."
nodes.em2_109: Rather than cutting her off, Sakaguchi asked a calm follow-up question:
nodes.em2_110: "Aside from loosening the isolation pads and risking contamination, what else concerns you here?"
nodes.em2_111: Seeing that he was genuinely weighing the operative risks, Mido added her second concern in rapid, clipped cadence:
nodes.em2_112: "The proximal wall is edematous and heavy, and that marginal straight vessel you just spared is delicate. Lowering both limbs and lifting them back up risks tugging the mesenteric border and putting a hematoma right into the terminal blood supply you worked to preserve."
nodes.em2_114: "That's a sharp catch. So we won't shift the proximal limb broadly—keep the proximal clamp anchored right where it sits on the isolation pad, cap both open lumens snugly with clean moist sponges, and let only the more mobile distal limb settle to its natural angle while I smooth the mesenteric fan from the root and check arterial pulsation and apposition tension without upward propping."
nodes.em2_115: Mido blinked once, her eyes following his logic down to the lighter, more mobile distal limb.
nodes.em2_116: "Easing only the distal side to trace the root... keeps the barrier intact and spares the proximal vessel any traction. So we're still verifying it your way?"
nodes.em2_117: "I'm the primary surgeon. Until I confirm with my own hands that the mesentery isn't twisted and the tension is reliable, I don't place the first stitch."
nodes.em2_118: A faint glint crossed Mido's eyes; without hesitation, she locked the proximal clamp steady and eased the distal limb smoothly downward.
nodes.em2_119: "Good. Proximal is anchored—check the distal side."
nodes.em2_120: Glancing over the tightly packed isolation layer, Sakaguchi issued a clear two-person division of labor:
nodes.em2_121: "Your concern is valid—the isolation plane cannot loosen, so we divide the task. Hiroko, two folded small moist sponges to cap both cut rims; Dr. Mido, hold the axis of both atraumatic clamps steady for me and take off only the upward lift while I trace the natural orientation segment by segment from the mesenteric root out to the cut edge."
nodes.em2_122: Hiroko passed the moist sponges at once:
nodes.em2_124: Sakaguchi wrapped both cut ends securely; seeing the thorough contamination safeguard in place, Mido dropped her insistence on placing stay sutures immediately and eased both clamps smoothly down toward their resting plane.
nodes.em2_125: Running his right hand gently from the mesenteric root out to both bowel ends, Sakaguchi looked up and gestured:
nodes.em2_126: "Now let's read it together—without thick pads forcing them up, let the two ends settle toward each other naturally. Look at the mesenteric lie, cut-edge color, and tension."
nodes.em2_127: Mido leaned in slightly for two seconds:
nodes.em2_128: "Natural apposition tension is plenty lax... though when the distal mesentery was propped high just now, the pad really was nudging a slight skew into it."
nodes.em2_129: "Then we lock in this corrected natural orientation, slip a single thin fresh isolation pad underneath, and begin the anastomosis."
nodes.em2_132: Once the artificial upward lift was removed and the mesentery smoothed from its root, the subtle difference stood out immediately—the distal mesentery, which had looked flush while propped on thick pads, really had carried a slight cant along the bolster; laid true now, the entire mesenteric fan lay flat and unstrained. Rechecking with both lumens securely capped and sterile isolation intact confirmed brisk vasa recta pulsations on both borders, vivid pink cut edges, and supple, unforced apposition.
nodes.em2_133: After slipping a fresh thin isolation pad underneath, just as Sakaguchi was about to ask Hiroko for the first stay suture, Mido—who had been studying both bowel ends intently—spoke up with an observation:
nodes.em2_134: "Sakaguchi. Look at the two lumen calibers—chronic obstruction has left the proximal end noticeably wider than the distal limb. If we sew them straight across end to end, closing the last corner is bound to bunch tissue pleats or leave a dog-ear angle."
nodes.em2_135: With atraumatic forceps, she lightly touched the antimesenteric border of the narrower distal bowel.
nodes.em2_136: "Before we place the stay sutures, Cheatle-trim the antimesenteric border of the narrower distal end on a gentle bevel to open the lumen slightly, then anchor the first seromuscular stitch at the mesenteric border. That matches the two calibers cleanly without touching mesenteric perfusion."
nodes.em2_137: Sakaguchi looked closely to verify the caliber mismatch between the proximal and distal openings, then reached out without hesitation for the Metzenbaum scissors:
nodes.em2_138: "Spot-on catch. We'll bevel the distal antimesenteric border just as you suggested—steady the distal clamp and underlying pad for me."
nodes.em2_140: Over the secure isolation pad, Sakaguchi tailored a modest oblique trim along the distal antimesenteric margin, dabbed away the bright arterial ooze along the fresh edge with a warm saline spongelet, and brought the once-mismatched bowel ends together into an even, seamless match.
nodes.em2_141: There was no contest of pride over who overruled whom—the primary surgeon had upheld a non-negotiable safety check, and within the framework of his call, his first assistant had supplied the exact technical refinement that made the anastomosis sounder.
nodes.em2_142: Over the fifteen minutes that followed, Operating Room 2 held only terse commands and the quiet click of steel.
nodes.em2_143: "3-0 silk, first stitch at the mesenteric border."
nodes.em2_147: Interrupted posterior seromuscular sutures, full-thickness inverting inner layer, then anterior seromuscular Lembert reinforcement—every bite width and needle depth from Sakaguchi stayed even and deliberate, while Mido's stay-suture tension and scissor timing across the table were a quiet pleasure to watch.
nodes.em2_148: "Second-to-last anterior stitch—give me a touch more room toward your side."
nodes.em2_151: The final seromuscular knot settled snug and was clipped clean, completing a warm, even anastomotic ring.
nodes.em2_152: With both atraumatic clamps released, luminal gas and fluid glided smoothly across the anastomosis from proximal to distal; palpating gently through the bowel wall between thumb and index finger, Sakaguchi confirmed a patent lumen admitting more than a full fingertip, rosy supple serosa, and zero leakage or blanching.
nodes.em2_153: Working in seamless tandem, the two then closed the underlying mesenteric defect with fine interrupted silk sutures, steering carefully clear of adjacent marginal vessels to prevent any postoperative internal hernia.
nodes.em2_154: With the bowel anastomosis and mesenteric closure complete, Hiroko cleared every lumen-contaminated instrument and kidney basin to an isolated off-table recovery zone; following protocol, Sakaguchi and Mido stripped off their outer gloves and donned fresh sterile gloves with Hiroko's assistance.
nodes.em2_155: In that brief lull as the table prepared warm normal saline for peritoneal irrigation, the female patient—who had been listening breathlessly from behind the sterile head screen—finally spoke up in a tentative voice.
nodes.em2_157: Moe leaned down promptly at the head of the table:
nodes.em2_158: "I'm right here. Are you feeling any fullness or chill anywhere?"
nodes.em2_159: "No, nothing hurts... I've just been wondering ever since I lay down here—is that really the strict Chief Mido from the inpatient ward standing across the table today? Listening from back here... it sounds like Dr. Sakaguchi has been giving the orders the whole time while Chief Mido assists him?"
nodes.em2_160: She swallowed, genuine apprehension creeping into her voice:
nodes.em2_161: "And a little while ago you two suddenly sounded so serious, and right after that you barely spoke at all... Did I accidentally overhear the two of you arguing at the operating table? Don't tell me my bowel was really hard to join back together..."
nodes.em2_162: At the head of the table, Moe blinked and opened her mouth to smooth things over—only for Emiko Mido to lift her head first from the field.
nodes.em2_163: Her voice was as level and unembellished as ever, free of bedside sugarcoating yet unmistakably steady in every word:
nodes.em2_164: "We weren't arguing. That was a normal intraoperative technical discussion."
nodes.em2_166: "Dr. Sakaguchi is the primary surgeon on this operation, and I am assisting him as first assistant. That was the scheduled assignment from the start."
nodes.em2_167: "Everything is proceeding according to plan. The narrowed segment has been removed, the bowel anastomosis is complete, and both perfusion and patency are very good."
nodes.em2_168: The patient went quiet for two seconds, clearly startled that the notoriously taciturn surgical chief from morning rounds had just explained things to her at such length.
nodes.em2_171: At the head end, Moe's eyes curved into a warm smile as she lightly squeezed the patient's hand and chimed in:
nodes.em2_172: "You can rest completely easy! Your blood pressure and heart rate on the monitor have been rock-steady from start to finish. The reason the two doctors spoke less and less just now—down to brief essential calls—is that their rhythm meshed so smoothly they didn't need extra words to get your bowel sewn up."
nodes.em2_173: Checking a freshly opened bottle of warm irrigation saline behind the back table, Hiroko added with an unhurried smile of her own:
nodes.em2_174: "That's right. Seeing Chief Mido say so little at the table while steadily holding suture scissors for the primary surgeon's knots is a rare sight even for someone who's worked these rooms as long as I have."
nodes.em2_175: Behind the drape, the patient let out a soft laugh of relief, the tension melting right out of her voice:
nodes.em2_176: "So that's what it was... Here I was sweating over nothing! I'll leave the rest in your hands, then, Dr. Sakaguchi and Chief Mido!"
nodes.em2_177: Beneath the surgical lamps, Sakaguchi held the suction-irrigator tip and cast an amused glance across at Emiko Mido.
nodes.em2_178: Without changing expression, Mido looked past his gaze and steadied the edge of a laparotomy pad:
nodes.em2_179: "What are you looking at me for? I only stated the facts."
nodes.em2_180: The corner of Sakaguchi's mouth lifted slightly:
nodes.em2_181: "Thanking my first assistant for steadying morale on the primary surgeon's behalf."
nodes.em2_182: "Spare me the banter. Finish irrigating so we can close."
nodes.em2_183: Once the warm saline was suctioned clear, the two surgeons ran a final joint inspection of the peritoneal cavity: the end-to-end small-bowel anastomosis sat pink and tension-free, the mesenteric defect was securely closed, every ligated pedicle was dry, and the bowel loops settled gently back into their natural anatomical lie.
nodes.em2_184: One by one, Sakaguchi and Mido withdrew the warm-saline protective laparotomy pads from around the wound and isolation zone, returning them to the counting area before sweeping the deep and superficial recesses once more to confirm a clean cavity.
nodes.em2_185: "Pre-closure count—all abdominal isolation and protective laparotomy pads removed; laparotomy pads, small gauze sponges, needles, bowel clamps, and all instruments verified correct on dual count with Nurse Honjo."
nodes.em2_187: With the count confirmed, Sakaguchi ran a continuous suture to close the peritoneum and posterior rectus sheath while Mido elevated the wound edges with crisp precision across from him; next they restored the rectus muscle to its bed and approximated the anterior rectus sheath and subcutaneous layer with interrupted stitches.
nodes.em2_188: As the final two skin sutures went in, the scrub and circulating sides completed their closing verification in unison:
nodes.em2_189: "Final end-of-case count—sponges, needles, and instruments all correct."
nodes.em2_191: Sakaguchi snugged down the final skin knot.
nodes.em2_193: Mido snipped the suture tails cleanly:
nodes.em2_195: A sterile dressing was smoothed neatly over the right abdominal incision. While Moe rechecked the patient's blood pressure and organized the IV lines at the head end for gurney transfer, Sakaguchi set down his forceps and looked across the table at Emiko Mido.
nodes.em2_196: "First time scrubbing in as my first assistant—what score is Chief Mido giving me today?"
nodes.em2_197: Mido lowered her lashes toward the neat incision dressing for a moment, then raised her eyes to him and delivered a single number:
nodes.em2_200: "Last time, assisting you earned me an eighty-five. Today I take primary, and it only goes up three points?"
nodes.em2_201: "It means you aren't entirely standing still."
nodes.em2_202: Keeping both gloved hands within the sterile zone at her chest, she lowered her voice so it carried cleanly between just the two of them:
nodes.em2_203: "Those extra three points aren't because your hands moved faster than last time."
nodes.em2_204: "They're because when your first assistant put forward a different approach, you neither deferred blindly just because I'm the surgical chief nor dug your heels in over a primary surgeon's pride—you took valid risk warnings seriously, explained your anatomical grounds clearly, and made the call while owning the consequences yourself."
nodes.em2_206: "What about the twelve points you took off? While we're still at the table, you might as well give me the rest."
nodes.em2_207: Mido gave him a cool look:
nodes.em2_208: "Before skin incision, you didn't brief your first assistant on the exploration and verification sequence you prefer—that's why our rhythm collided when I flipped the loop early. If the primary surgeon has his own method, he states the coordination order before picking up the knife. As for the rest of the margin, an elective benign small-bowel anastomosis simply isn't complex enough to hand out ninety-plus."
nodes.em2_210: "Noted. Next time I'll lay out the sequence before skin incision—and collect the remaining points from you when a major case lands on the board."
nodes.em2_211: "That depends on whether you're good enough to take them."
nodes.em2_213: "Earning three extra points from Chief Mido is no small feat—I'll gladly take an eighty-eight."
nodes.em2_214: "Satisfied with eighty-eight? I assumed you'd set your own bar at ninety or higher."
nodes.em2_215: "If it jumped too fast all at once, what would be left to climb next time we scrub in together?"
nodes.em2_216: Mido gave a quiet hum without arguing:
nodes.em2_217: "...At least you know where you stand."
nodes.em2_218: Looking into her cool brow above the mask, Sakaguchi tossed back a light question:
nodes.em2_219: "Now that the primary surgeon has his score—care to hear how I'd grade my first assistant today?"
nodes.em2_222: "Minus two points for jumping half a beat ahead of my sequence at the start, earned back on that call to bevel the distal antimesenteric border—call it a grudging ninety-five."
nodes.em2_223: Mido shot him a cool sideways glance:
nodes.em2_224: "You're certainly the first primary surgeon at Hoshimi Hospital bold enough to dock me two points."
nodes.em2_225: Cool as her words were, there wasn't a trace of real displeasure in her eyes.
nodes.em2_226: Confirming the incision dressing was secure, Sakaguchi and Mido removed the sterile drapes covering the patient, stepped back out of the sterile field, and stripped off their outer sterile gowns and gloves into the disposal hamper in sequence.
nodes.em2_227: At the same time, Moe finished verifying the patient's stable vital signs and epidural catheter fixation at the head end, wheeling up the transfer gurney alongside the ward orderly for a smooth lateral transfer.
nodes.em2_228: As the gurney rolled past the table, the patient turned her head specifically toward the two surgeons with a grateful smile:
nodes.em2_229: "Thank you, Dr. Sakaguchi—and thank you too, Chief Mido!"
nodes.em2_230: "Get plenty of rest back on the ward. Follow the fasting and IV orders for the first couple of days until flatus returns—we'll come check on you during rounds."
nodes.em2_231: Mido gave a slight nod toward the gurney as well:
nodes.em2_232: "Rest well, and keep strain off your abdomen."
nodes.em2_233: Once Moe had escorted the patient safely out of the room and Hiroko had wheeled away the pathology specimen and instrument recovery cart, the two surgeons stepped out of the operating room to wash their hands and change back into their everyday white coats.
nodes.em2_234: The corridor outside the fourth-floor surgical suite was quiet and immaculate, afternoon sunlight slanting across the pale grey floor.
nodes.em2_235: When Sakaguchi stepped out past the wash area carrying the freshly signed operative record binder, he spotted Emiko Mido—already changed back into a crisp white coat—standing by the corridor window as though she had waited half a minute specifically for him.
nodes.em2_237: "I've finished writing up the operative note. Left the first-assistant signature line open for you."
nodes.em2_238: Taking the clipboard, Mido scanned the anastomosis details and count record with brisk precision, uncapped her fountain pen, signed her name cleanly, and handed the binder back.
nodes.em2_239: Sakaguchi took the binder and was about to excuse himself to check on the ward when Mido suddenly called out to him.
nodes.em2_241: Sakaguchi's step slowed as he turned back toward her:
nodes.em2_243: Meeting his eyes, Mido kept her expression as cool and matter-of-fact as if discussing routine roster business, pausing only half a beat before continuing:
nodes.em2_244: "Going forward on the regular surgical schedule—whether you're leading a case and need a first assistant, or facing a difficult case that calls for a partner—you don't need to steer clear of my name."
nodes.em2_245: Sakaguchi raised an eyebrow slightly, catching the full weight of that permission:
nodes.em2_246: "Sounds like scrubbing in as first assistant today wasn't completely boring for Chief Mido?"
nodes.em2_247: Slipping her fountain pen back into her breast pocket, Mido shifted her gaze calmly down the corridor ahead.
nodes.em2_249: She stepped past him, leaving only two cool, faintly challenging lines in the instant their shoulders passed:
nodes.em2_252: Watching that poised white-coated figure walk steadily away down the corridor, Sakaguchi glanced down at the two names signed side by side on the operative record and let out a quiet smile.
nodes.em2_254: From today onward at Hoshimi Hospital's operating tables, the most demanding surgical chief in the department was truly standing where they could fight side by side.
